title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The AI Office's decision outlines the organization’s approach to implementing and overseeing artificial intelligence technologies, emphasizing safety, transparency, and ethical use. It establishes guidelines for developers, users, and stakeholders to ensure responsible AI deployment and compliance with regulatory standards.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: The policy outlines the open positions for technology specialists in AI, detailing their responsibilities, required qualifications, and how they will contribute to the organization’s AI initiatives. It also explains the hiring process, training expectations, and the role these specialists will play in supporting and advancing AI projects.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The AI Office is currently seeking a Lead Scientific Adviser to fill a vacant position. This role will guide AI research initiatives, uphold policy standards, and promote scientific integrity within the organization.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: This policy announces a vacancy for Legal Officers in the AI office. It outlines the role’s responsibilities, required qualifications, and application procedure.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: This policy explains how AI office vacancies are managed, highlighting the responsibilities of policy officers in overseeing transitions. It sets out procedures, selection criteria, and communication steps to ensure a smooth handover and continued operation.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel reviews and advises on the European Union’s regulatory framework for artificial intelligence, ensuring that AI systems are developed and deployed safely and responsibly. It focuses on balancing the need for innovation with safeguards for transparency, accountability, and fundamental rights.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This policy document proposes a request to develop standardised practices or protocols. It likely urges the creation and adoption of uniform guidelines to ensure consistency, transparency, and safety in the relevant field.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This notice announces a public consultation on a new Community of Practice (CoP) policy. It invites stakeholders to review and provide feedback on the proposed guidelines before they are finalized.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document invites individuals or organizations to express interest in joining a Community of Practice (CoP). It explains the process for submitting expressions of interest and outlines the goals and benefits of participating in the CoP.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: The policy document explains how a Community of Practice collaborates to create and refine drafts through repeated cycles of writing, reviewing, and revising. It emphasizes transparency, collective expertise, and continuous improvement to ensure policies accurately reflect shared goals and stakeholder input.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: This policy outlines the sequence of steps taken to draft the CoP (Community of Practice) guidelines, showing key milestones and dates. It helps stakeholders understand when each phase began, progressed, and was finalized.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document is a first draft of a Code of Practice that outlines the principles and guidelines for responsible AI usage. It aims to set standards for development, deployment, and oversight to ensure AI systems are ethical, safe, and aligned with societal values.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 2nd Draft is an updated set of guidelines for responsible AI development and deployment, focusing on ethical standards, transparency, and accountability. It offers organizations a framework to align their AI strategies with emerging regulations and best practices, helping to build trust and ensure compliance.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: The third draft of the Code of Practice establishes clear, actionable guidelines for the responsible use, development, and governance of AI systems, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and stakeholder engagement. It also sets out compliance requirements, risk management procedures, and a framework for ongoing review to adapt to evolving AI technologies and societal needs.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft is a proposed framework designed to guide the responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence. It emphasizes collaboration among stakeholders, sets safety and ethical standards, and seeks to balance innovation with public trust.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is a formal agreement that sets out shared commitments to develop and use artificial intelligence responsibly and safely. It brings together stakeholders to promote transparency, accountability, and cooperation in addressing the societal impacts of AI.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: These guidelines define which AI practices are not allowed, such as creating harmful, misleading, or discriminatory systems. They aim to protect users and society by setting clear boundaries on how AI can be developed and deployed.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: This document explains how to define an artificial intelligence system, outlining key characteristics, scope, and examples. It provides clear criteria and terminology for distinguishing AI from non‑AI technologies to ensure consistent application across organizations.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy aims to strengthen the communication and collaboration around start-ups and innovative projects. It proposes initiatives to support entrepreneurs, share best practices, and create a more dynamic innovation ecosystem.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups aims to give early‑stage technology companies across Europe access to high‑performance computing resources and tailored support. It provides shared HPC infrastructure, training, and collaboration opportunities to help startups develop and scale AI and other data‑intensive applications.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This policy outlines the approach and best practices for managing risks associated with the use and deployment of AI technologies. It highlights key risk areas, mitigation strategies, and responsibilities for stakeholders to ensure responsible AI implementation.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This video is a webinar that explains the fundamentals of risk management. It covers how to identify, assess, and mitigate risks in different settings.
